newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish seabed survey will help oil, gas exploration.
newsitem.headline: Irish seabed survey will help oil, gas exploration.

text.p: A recent sonar survey of the seabed west of Ireland will be of major importance to oil and gas exploration in the area although it will be a year before the results are analysed, Ireland's Marine Institute said.
A survey ship was used a sophisticated long-range sonar system to map an area of 200,000 square km around the Rockall Trough over 25 days.

"The information produced provides a three-dimensional map of the seabed, which is of vital interest to fishermen, oceanographers and those involved in underwater oil and gas exploration," the Marine Institute said.
The survey will produce high definition seismic profiles, and identify priority areas for oil and gas exploration, it said.

"The new sonar equipent allows you to survey a large area very quickly and identify the areas that you will focus on in the future," said Geoffrey O'Sullivan, the Marine Institute's development manager.

"We have a lot of new information about the Rockall Trough area which will be of interest to the oil and gas industry, but we won't know until we process it exactly how it will help," he told Reuters.
O'Sullivan said only a fifth of Ireland's continental shelf area had been surveyed in the project and he hoped more would be covered in future.
The project was supported by the Marine Institute and was carried out by a team which included representatives of the Petroleum Affairs Division of the Irish government.
